_comment: WHAT THE GAME TEACHES ABOUT ITSELF, and when.
Level 1 is the tutorial and it was never teaching anything. The controls screen
under the pause menu is a REFERENCE — a player has to already suspect a verb
exists before they will go looking for it there — and ActionPromptHUD shows four
key caps (R, Q, E, F) with no words around them. Movement, jumping, the mouse that
does all of placement, the bag, and the fact that a drawing is on a clock were
never said anywhere. Lolo is standing right there and is the reason the game has a
guide at all, so he says them.
EVERY LESSON GOES TO THE HINT BAR, NEVER THE DIALOGUE BOX. The bar does not stop
the world, needs no key press and clears itself. A tutorial that pauses the game to
tell you how to walk is the thing this file exists to stop.
KEYS ARE NOT WRITTEN HERE. `{keys}` is filled at runtime from the live InputMap via
ControlsOverlay.keys_for, so a rebinding cannot leave a lesson naming a key that no
longer does anything — the same split controls.json already makes, for the same
reason. Use `action` for one key, plus `through` for a contiguous block (the six
inventory slots are one idea to the player, not six), or `keys` to name something
the InputMap does not hold, which is the whole mouse.
`at` is the moment the lesson is offered; the director spends each one once per run.
`after` holds a lesson back until another has been seen, so the order survives a
player who does things out of sequence.
NO LESSON MAY NAME A DRAWABLE CLASS. Same rule as the dialogue, and it bites harder
here than anywhere: `key` and `door` are both classes in the roster and both are the
answer to a Level 1 route, so a lesson saying 'press this key' would be naming a
solution in the one place the player is guaranteed to read. Say `{keys}` and let the
cap speak.

A lesson with an `anchor` is taught in a TutorialCallout beside that control instead of in the hint bar. `side` is a preference; auto picks whichever side has room. An anchor the level cannot resolve falls back to the bar rather than being dropped -- an unteachable lesson is worse than an unpointed one.
Anchor names are the tutorial's own vocabulary, resolved by LevelBase._tutorial_target. They are deliberately NOT node paths: rename a HUD node and that one function changes.

canvas_briefing is Lolo's explanation of the drawing screen, said in a dialogue box INSIDE the panel the first time it is opened. It is the one place the tutorial stops the world, and it costs nothing because the panel is a modal and the world is already stopped. Omit it and the canvas opens straight to the paper.

The morph card top right carries two readings the game showed and never explained: how long this drawing has left, and how sure the recogniser was of it. `clock` waits for `morph_running` rather than `became_creature` -- two seconds into a ten-second life -- because `revert` already has that frame and one callout at a time is the rule. `sure` then waits on `clock` and not on `revert`: it only has to avoid landing on top of the other reading, and hanging it off a lesson that may itself be deferred (a revert prompt that has not been built, a busy bar) means it can be deferred twice.

lessons.text: Her brush is in here. {keys} opens it.
{keys} takes it back, and the ink with it.
That bar is the drawing's life, apo. It runs out.
The number beside it is how sure I was of your drawing.
It is going, apo. A drawing does not last.
In your bag. {keys} brings it out.
{keys} and I will read it again.
Stand at it and hold {keys}, apo. That is how you go up.
That word is what it needs DONE, not what to draw.
That cost ink, apo. There is not much of it.
You begin here now, not at the start.

canvas_briefing: Her canvas, apo. What you draw on it, this place believes.
Draw with the mouse. The ink is measured — do not waste it.
Then Transform. I will say what I think it is, and how sure I am.
If I am not sure enough I will say so, and it costs you nothing.
